title: caller handles recursion between smime-tree and mime-tree; neither crate recurses into the other
description: smime-tree.decrypt() returns raw inner MIME bytes. If those bytes are themselves S/MIME, the caller calls smime-tree.decrypt() again. Neither crate auto-recurses. A future contributor might suggest adding auto-unwrap logic inside decrypt() or parse() to 'handle the common case'. That would be wrong for two reasons: (1) it creates unbounded recursion depth with no caller-controlled limit, which is a DoS surface; (2) it couples the two crates in a way that violates the stated dependency direction (mime-tree must not depend on smime-tree). The caller-loop model gives the caller full control over recursion depth, logging, and error handling at each layer.
